needs: Real numbers on a chart: three curves plotted from computed values as the input grows.

brief.title: n, n log n and n squared, plotted
brief.idea: As the input grows, n squared pulls away from n log n and n, so a quadratic algorithm that is fine for a hundred items is hopeless for a million.

beats.say: Three ways to sort a list take n steps, n log n steps, and n squared steps. Start with ten items.
beats.show: A table appears with three rows, n, n log n and n squared, and one column for n = 10.

beats.say: That is ten, about thirty three, and one hundred steps. At this size the difference hardly matters at all.
At a hundred items it is one hundred, about six hundred and sixty four, and ten thousand.
beats.show: A second column for n = 100 fills in: 100, 664 and 10,000.

beats.say: Plot all three, and the n squared curve already climbs far above the other two.
beats.show: A chart appears with n along the bottom up to 100 and steps up the side; three curves are drawn and n squared rises steeply.

beats.say: At a thousand items, n log n is about ten thousand, while n squared reaches a million.
beats.show: The bottom axis extends to 1,000 and the side axis rescales; n squared towers over the other two, which lie almost flat.

beats.say: Now take a million items, say every song in a large music library, on a machine doing a billion steps a second.
beats.show: A heading reads n = 1,000,000 with a note of 1 billion steps per second.

beats.say: n log n is about twenty million steps: two hundredths of a second.
beats.show: The n log n row shows 20 million and 0.02 s.

beats.say: n squared is a trillion steps: about seventeen minutes of waiting, for the very same list.
beats.show: The n squared row shows 1 trillion and 17 minutes, beside the 0.02 seconds.

beats.say: Small inputs hide the gap. Large inputs make the shape of the curve the only thing that counts.
beats.show: The chart returns with the three curves labelled, and the gap between n squared and n log n is highlighted.

beats.say: So when the input can grow large, choosing n log n over n squared is the difference between instant and unusable.
beats.show: Two notes sit beside the curves: 0.02 seconds next to n log n, and 17 minutes next to n squared.
